S29.title: Already taking a paracetamol combination
S29.complaint: I'm taking a cold and flu tablet but my headache is still there. Can I add some paracetamol?

answers.symptoms: Runny nose, mild headache, slight temperature. No stiff neck, rash or breathing problems.
answers.meds: A cold and flu combination tablet — the label says paracetamol, phenylephrine and chlorphenamine. Four times a day.

S29.seeDoctor: if symptoms worsen or last more than a week
S29.learning: Duplicate ingredients are a common cause of accidental overdose. Many cold & flu products contain paracetamol — always check the full ingredient list.
adviceOptions: Your cold tablet already contains paracetamol, so taking more could exceed the safe daily limit. Keep to the label dose, rest and drink fluids; see a doctor if you feel worse or it lasts beyond a week.
Paracetamol is very safe, so you can take extra tablets on top of the cold & flu product.
Double your cold & flu tablets for a day to clear the headache faster.

S30.title: Headache in pregnancy
S30.complaint: I have a headache. Can I take ibuprofen?

answers.symptoms: Mild headache. No blurred vision or flashing lights, no sudden swelling of my face or hands, no tummy pain.
answers.meds: Just pregnancy vitamins with folic acid.

S30.seeDoctor: and let your midwife know so your blood pressure can be checked — seek urgent care for a severe headache, visual disturbances, or sudden swelling of the face, hands or feet
S30.learning: NSAIDs such as ibuprofen are generally avoided in pregnancy unless prescribed. Paracetamol at the lowest effective dose is usually preferred. Severe headache with visual symptoms or swelling may signal pre-eclampsia.

S31.title: Heartburn in pregnancy
S31.complaint: I get heartburn every evening. Is there something safe I can take?

answers.duration: A few weeks — it started in the third trimester.
answers.symptoms: Burning after meals and when lying down. No vomiting, no severe upper tummy pain, no headache or vision changes.

S31.seeDoctor: and mention it to your midwife; seek urgent care for severe upper abdominal pain, headache or vision changes
S31.learning: Heartburn is common in pregnancy; antacids and alginates are commonly used first-line. Acid-reducing tablets should be checked with the doctor.

S32.title: Penicillin allergy — amoxicillin prescription
S32.complaint: Here's my prescription from the clinic. I need these antibiotics.

answers.duration: The doctor diagnosed a chest infection yesterday.
answers.symptoms: Cough with fever. No severe breathlessness.
answers.allergies: Yes — penicillin gives me a rash and swelling. I don't think I told the doctor.

S32.learning: Always check allergies before dispensing, even with a valid prescription. A penicillin allergy means amoxicillin must not be given; contact the prescriber for an alternative.
adviceOptions: Amoxicillin is a penicillin, and you've reacted to penicillin before. I can't dispense this safely — I'll contact your prescriber so they can choose a suitable alternative today.
It's a different brand, so the allergy won't matter. Take it as prescribed.
Take half the dose to reduce the chance of a reaction.

rx.directions: 1 capsule three times daily for 5 days

S33.title: Elderly customer wants sleeping pills
S33.complaint: I can't sleep well these days. Give me some sleeping tablets.

answers.symptoms: I wake up at night to pass urine and can't get back to sleep. No low mood, no pain, no breathing problems at night.
answers.meds: Tablets for my prostate and for blood pressure.
answers.history: Enlarged prostate and high blood pressure.
answers.lifestyle: I drink tea in the evening and nap in the afternoon.

S33.seeDoctor: if poor sleep continues, or the night-time urination gets worse
S33.learning: Sedating antihistamines (e.g., diphenhydramine) are generally not recommended for older adults due to anticholinergic effects, confusion and falls risk. Address causes and sleep hygiene.
adviceOptions: Sedating sleep aids can cause confusion, falls and urinary problems in older adults, especially with prostate issues. Let's try sleep-hygiene steps — less evening tea, shorter naps, a regular bedtime — and see your doctor if it continues, as the night-time urination should be reviewed.
Take two antihistamine sleep tablets every night; they're harmless.
Borrow a friend's prescription sleeping pills for a few nights.

S34.title: Knee pain — stomach ulcer history
S34.complaint: My knee aches after walking. I want some painkiller tablets.

answers.symptoms: Aching knee after activity. No redness, no hot swollen joint, no injury, no fever.
answers.history: I had a stomach ulcer that bled two years ago.

S34.seeDoctor: if the knee becomes hot, red and swollen, you can't bear weight, or the pain keeps getting worse
S34.learning: Oral NSAIDs and aspirin are avoided after a peptic ulcer/GI bleed. Paracetamol or a topical NSAID (low systemic exposure) are commonly considered instead.

S35.title: Toothache — patient on lithium
S35.complaint: I have a toothache. Can I get ibuprofen until I see the dentist?

answers.symptoms: Throbbing tooth. No facial swelling, no fever, no difficulty swallowing or opening my mouth.

S35.seeDoctor: and book a dentist appointment soon — go urgently for facial swelling, fever or difficulty swallowing
S35.learning: NSAIDs can raise lithium levels and cause toxicity. Paracetamol is preferred, and dental pain needs a dentist.

S36.title: Graze — iodine allergy
S36.complaint: I fell off my bike and scraped my elbow. I need something to clean it.

answers.symptoms: Surface graze, a little gravel I've rinsed out. No deep cut, I can move my arm fine.
answers.lifestyle: Tetanus jab is up to date.

S36.seeDoctor: if the wound shows signs of infection, or dirt can't be removed
S36.learning: Always ask about allergies before recommending antiseptics. Povidone-iodine should be avoided in people with iodine sensitivity.

S37.title: Teenager with fever — aspirin request
S37.complaint: My 15-year-old daughter has a fever and body aches. Can I give her aspirin?

answers.symptoms: Fever 38.2 °C, body aches, sore throat. No rash, no stiff neck, she's drinking fluids.

S37.seeDoctor: if the fever lasts more than 3 days, or she develops a rash, stiff neck, severe sore throat with difficulty swallowing, or confusion
S37.learning: Aspirin is not given to anyone under 16 because of the risk of Reye's syndrome. Paracetamol or ibuprofen are suitable alternatives when there are no contraindications.

S38.title: Child with cough
S38.complaint: My 4-year-old has a cough. Can I give her a cough suppressant syrup?

answers.symptoms: Dry cough, runny nose. She's eating and playing. No breathing difficulty, no high fever, no wheeze.

S38.seeDoctor: if she has breathing difficulty, a high fever, or the cough lasts more than 3 weeks
S38.learning: Many OTC cough suppressants are not recommended for young children. Simple soothing remedies (e.g., honey for children over 1 year) and fluids are preferred.
adviceOptions: For young children, cough suppressants aren't recommended. Warm drinks, honey (over age 1) and rest usually help; see a doctor if she has breathing difficulty, high fever or the cough lasts more than 3 weeks.
Give her an adult cough suppressant at half dose.
Antibiotics will stop the cough quickly.

S39.title: Chest pain disguised as indigestion
S39.complaint: I've got bad indigestion. Can I have an antacid?

answers.symptoms: It's a heavy pressure in my chest spreading to my left arm and jaw. I feel sweaty and a bit sick.
answers.lifestyle: I was climbing stairs when it started.

S39.learning: Chest pressure spreading to the arm or jaw with sweating or nausea may indicate a heart attack. Call emergency services immediately — never treat as indigestion.
adviceOptions: These symptoms could be a heart problem. Please sit down — I'm calling emergency services right now. This needs urgent hospital care, not an antacid.
Take this antacid and come back tomorrow if it hasn't settled.
Walk around a bit to see if the pain goes away.

S40.title: Sudden severe headache
S40.complaint: I need your strongest painkiller. My head is killing me.

answers.duration: It came on suddenly about an hour ago — like being hit on the head.
answers.symptoms: It's the worst headache of my life. My neck is stiff and I've vomited twice. Light hurts my eyes.

S40.learning: A "thunderclap" (sudden, worst-ever) headache, especially with a stiff neck, vomiting or light sensitivity, is a medical emergency.
adviceOptions: A sudden, severe headache with a stiff neck and vomiting needs emergency assessment. I'm calling an ambulance. Please lie down here while we wait, and don't take any painkillers in the meantime.
Take two strong painkillers and lie down in a dark room.
It's probably a migraine; come back if it happens again.

S41.title: Fever in a young infant
S41.complaint: My 2-month-old baby has a temperature. Can I get some infant paracetamol drops?

answers.symptoms: His temperature is 38.4 °C. He's feeding less than usual and sleepier.
answers.lifestyle: He had his first vaccines last week.

S41.learning: Any infant under 3 months with a fever of 38 °C or higher must be urgently assessed by a doctor. Do not simply sell an antipyretic.
adviceOptions: Babies under 3 months with a temperature of 38 °C or more need to be seen by a doctor urgently today. Please take him to a doctor or emergency department now.
Give the drops every 4 hours and wait a few days.
Wrap him in warm blankets to sweat out the fever.

S42.title: Persistent cough with weight loss
S42.complaint: I need a strong cough syrup. This cough just won't go away.

answers.symptoms: I've lost weight without trying, I sweat at night, and sometimes there's a little blood in my phlegm.
answers.meds: I tried two cough syrups already.
answers.lifestyle: I live in a crowded hostel.

S42.learning: A cough lasting more than 2–3 weeks, especially with weight loss, night sweats or blood, requires medical evaluation (e.g., for tuberculosis or other serious causes).
adviceOptions: A cough lasting this long with weight loss, night sweats and blood in the phlegm must be checked by a doctor promptly — it needs tests, not another cough syrup.
Try this stronger cough syrup for another two weeks.
It's probably just a smoker's cough; ignore it.

S43.title: Bloody diarrhoea with fever
S43.complaint: I have bad diarrhoea. Can I get loperamide to stop it?

answers.symptoms: There's blood in the stool and I have a high fever. Severe cramps.
answers.lifestyle: I came back from a trip last week.

S43.learning: Bloody diarrhoea and/or high fever are red flags. Antimotility drugs like loperamide should not be used; refer for medical assessment.
adviceOptions: Blood in the stool with a high fever needs to be seen by a doctor today. Loperamide isn't suitable here. Keep sipping fluids or ORS on the way.
Loperamide will stop it — take double the dose.
Avoid all fluids until the diarrhoea stops.

S44.title: Antibiotics for a cold
S44.complaint: Just give me some antibiotics, I have a cold. I don't have time for a doctor.

answers.symptoms: Runny nose, sore throat, mild temperature. No breathing difficulty, no ear pain, no severe throat pain.

S44.seeDoctor: if you develop breathing difficulty, ear or severe throat pain, or symptoms last more than 10 days
S44.learning: Antibiotics do not work against viral infections like colds, and supplying prescription-only antibiotics without a prescription is unsafe and non-compliant. Offer symptomatic relief.
adviceOptions: Colds are caused by viruses, so antibiotics won't help and need a prescription. Rest, fluids and symptom relief are best; see a doctor if you get breathing difficulty, ear pain or it lasts over 10 days.
I'll give you leftover antibiotics from another customer.
Antibiotics will make the cold go away in a day.

S45.title: Changing mole
S45.complaint: I have a mole on my back that's itchy. Can you give me a cream?

answers.duration: I noticed it changing over the last two months.
answers.symptoms: It's got bigger, the edge is irregular, it has two colours now and it bled once.
answers.history: I had bad sunburns as a child.

S45.learning: Changes in a mole (asymmetry, irregular border, colour change, increasing size, bleeding) require prompt medical assessment for possible skin cancer.
adviceOptions: A mole that's changing in size, shape or colour, or bleeding, should be checked by a doctor soon. A cream isn't appropriate until it has been assessed.
Use hydrocortisone cream on it for a month.
Try to remove it yourself at home.

S46.title: Non-healing diabetic foot wound
S46.complaint: I have a small sore on my foot. I need an antiseptic cream.

answers.duration: About two weeks — it isn't healing.
answers.symptoms: The skin around it is red and warm, and I can't feel my toes well.

S46.learning: Foot wounds in people with diabetes can deteriorate quickly due to poor circulation and reduced sensation. Refer promptly.
adviceOptions: With diabetes, a foot wound that isn't healing and looks red needs to be seen by a doctor or foot clinic promptly — today if possible. Please don't rely on a cream alone.
Apply this antiseptic for a few more weeks and see.
Soak the foot in very hot water every day.

S47.title: Bee sting with throat swelling
S47.complaint: A bee stung me ten minutes ago. Can I get an antihistamine?

answers.symptoms: My lips are swelling, my throat feels tight and it's getting hard to breathe. I feel dizzy.
answers.allergies: I had a big reaction to a sting once before.

S47.learning: Swelling of the lips/throat, breathing difficulty or dizziness after a sting suggests anaphylaxis — call emergency services and use adrenaline if available. Antihistamines alone are not enough.
adviceOptions: This looks like a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis). I'm calling emergency services now. If you carry an adrenaline auto-injector, use it immediately.
Take an antihistamine tablet and wait to see if it settles.
Put some calamine lotion on the sting.

S48.title: Heartburn with difficulty swallowing
S48.complaint: I need something for my heartburn. The usual antacids aren't working.

answers.symptoms: Food feels like it gets stuck when I swallow, and I've lost weight without trying.
answers.meds: I've been taking antacids every day.

S48.learning: Alarm features with dyspepsia (difficulty swallowing, weight loss, vomiting, GI bleeding, persistent symptoms in older adults) require medical referral.
adviceOptions: Difficulty swallowing and unexplained weight loss are alarm symptoms. You need to see a doctor soon for investigations rather than continue antacids.
Switch to a stronger antacid and keep taking it for a few more months.
Eat softer food and ignore it.

S49.title: Painful red eye with blurred vision
S49.complaint: My eye is red. Can I have some eye drops?

answers.symptoms: It's very painful, my vision is blurry in that eye, and light really hurts.
answers.lifestyle: I sometimes sleep with my lenses in.

S49.learning: Red-eye red flags: pain, reduced vision, photophobia, contact-lens wear. These need urgent same-day eye assessment.
adviceOptions: A painful red eye with blurred vision and light sensitivity — especially with contact lenses — needs urgent eye assessment today. Remove your lenses and go to an eye casualty or emergency department.
Use lubricant drops for a week and see.
Keep wearing your contact lenses to protect the eye.

S50.title: Asthma reliever not working
S50.complaint: I need a new inhaler, mine isn't working. I can't catch my breath.

answers.duration: It got worse over the last hour.
answers.symptoms: I'm very breathless, I can't finish sentences, and my lips look a bit blue. My reliever isn't helping.
answers.meds: Blue reliever inhaler — I've used it many times today.

S50.learning: Inability to complete sentences, worsening breathlessness and poor response to a reliever indicate a severe asthma attack — an emergency.
adviceOptions: This sounds like a severe asthma attack. I'm calling emergency services now. Sit upright, and keep using your reliever as your asthma plan directs while we wait.
Here's a cough syrup; go home and rest.
Come back tomorrow with a prescription.

S51.title: Valid metformin prescription
S51.complaint: I've been newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. Here is my prescription.

answers.symptoms: I feel fine now.
answers.history: Type 2 diabetes. My doctor checked my kidney function.

S51.seeDoctor: if you have persistent vomiting, severe stomach upset, or feel very unwell
S51.learning: For a valid prescription: verify the patient, prescriber, date, drug, strength and directions; check allergies and interactions, then counsel (metformin is taken with meals to reduce stomach upset).

S52.title: Requested brand out of stock
S52.complaint: Can I get {BRAND}? It's for my hay fever.

answers.duration: Hay fever season — a few days.
answers.symptoms: Sneezing, runny nose. No wheeze.
answers.lifestyle: I take the bus to work.

S52.seeDoctor: if you develop wheezing or breathlessness
S52.learning: When a requested brand is out of stock, a generic alternative with the same active ingredient, strength and dosage form can usually be offered (in line with local rules), explaining it to the customer.

S53.title: Elderly customer — multiple medicines
S53.complaint: I have a cold. Give me your strongest cold and flu tablets.

answers.symptoms: Blocked nose, aches, mild temperature. No breathlessness or chest pain.
answers.history: High blood pressure and type 2 diabetes.

S53.seeDoctor: if you become breathless, develop chest pain or confusion, or don't improve within a week
S53.learning: Combination cold products often contain decongestants (raise blood pressure) and sedating antihistamines (falls risk in older adults). Choose single-ingredient options matched to symptoms.

S54.title: Out-of-date prescription
S54.complaint: Can you fill this prescription? I didn't get it filled before.

answers.duration: The prescription is from earlier this year.
answers.symptoms: I have a sore throat again now.

S54.learning: Prescriptions have a validity period and are written for a specific clinical situation. Out-of-date prescriptions must not be dispensed; refer to the prescriber.
adviceOptions: This prescription is out of date and was written for a past illness. I can't dispense it — please see your doctor so your current symptoms can be assessed.
I'll dispense it since the drug name is still correct.
Take the antibiotics for just three days instead.

rx.directions: 1 capsule three times daily for 7 days
rx.issue: Dated about 9 months ago — beyond a typical validity period

S55.title: Breathless smoker wants cough syrup
S55.complaint: My cough syrup isn't working. I need something stronger.

answers.symptoms: I'm more breathless than usual, my ankles are swollen, and I have to sleep propped up on pillows.
answers.history: High blood pressure, heart attack 5 years ago.

S55.learning: A cough with breathlessness, orthopnoea (needing to sleep propped up) and ankle swelling in someone with heart disease may indicate heart failure — refer promptly.
adviceOptions: Breathlessness, ankle swelling and needing extra pillows with your heart history need a doctor's assessment today — a cough syrup won't treat the cause.
Here's a stronger cough syrup — use it for another week.
Drink more water and lie flat to rest.

S56.title: Valid prescription — check interactions
S56.complaint: My doctor started me on a cholesterol tablet. Here's the prescription.

answers.symptoms: No symptoms.
answers.lifestyle: I drink grapefruit juice every morning.

S56.seeDoctor: if you get unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness — and avoid large amounts of grapefruit juice
S56.learning: Dispense valid prescriptions after checks, and counsel: report unexplained muscle pain; avoid large quantities of grapefruit juice with atorvastatin.
